test_title: PYST 22: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 14 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Capital account convertibility refers to free movement of capital across borders. Which of the following committees recommended full capital account convertibility?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tarapore Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tarapore Committee was established by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 1997 under the chairmanship of S.S. Tarapore to recommend measures for full capital account convertibility in India.
 
• Capital account convertibility refers to the ability to freely move capital (foreign investments, loans, etc.) across borders without restrictions.
 
• The committee submitted its report in 1997, outlining a phased approach to achieve full capital account convertibility.
 
• The Tarapore Committee emphasized prerequisites such as fiscal consolidation, inflation control, and strengthening the financial sector to ensure stability during capital account liberalization.
 
• Its recommendations were considered crucial for India's gradual integration into the global financial system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Account Convertibility:**

 
 
• It enables residents and foreign entities to conduct financial transactions like investments, lending, and borrowing freely across borders.
 
• Full convertibility can boost foreign investments, trade, and economic growth but may increase financial risks during global instability.
 
 
 
• **Preconditions for Capital Account Convertibility:**
 
 
• Fiscal deficit should be reduced to sustainable levels.
 
• Inflation should be maintained within a reasonable range.
 
• Financial sector reforms and robust regulatory mechanisms are necessary to avoid systemic risks.
 
 
 
• **Rangarajan Committee:**
 
 
• Headed by Dr. C. Rangarajan, it focused on banking and financial sector reforms in India.
 
• While important, it did not specifically address capital account convertibility like the Tarapore Committee.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Full Capital Account Convertibility:**
 
 
• It enhances global integration and competitiveness of domestic financial markets.
 
• However, it can expose the economy to volatile capital flows and financial crises if not managed cautiously.
